Key is Pose: Melody and Instrument Identity in a Thousand-Brains System with a Verified Cochlear Sensor

B. Leavelle · with two instances of Claude (one at the bench, one reading the tables)

ear bit-verified vs google/carfac runtime 0.15–0.30× realtime, live in a DAW verdicts 12/12 stable under unit surgery data self-recorded, two guitars, on disk

Abstract (draft bullets — tighten last)

We gave Numenta's Monty (Thousand Brains Project) its first auditory sensor: Lyon's CARFAC cochlea plus the Stabilized Auditory Image (SAI), ported to run live in a DAW and verified against the published reference to floating-point precision. Sounds become trajectories through an auditory reference frame (log-lag × cochlear place), and Monty's existing object-learning machinery — built for vision and touch — learns and recognizes them unchanged.

Headline results, all on self-recorded guitar: a melody recognized in a key never heard in training (transposition = translation, measured at +3.0 semitones exact); recognition surviving a change of instrument at the same fit as a re-take (78% vs 76% ceiling); and a pre-registered prediction suite in which the guitar's resonant body — not the musical mode — turned out to carry the identity-breaking signal ("mode is identity": overturned by controlled retake).

Take-to-take variance in the player's hands exceeded the effect of transposition. The key you play it in matters less than which take it was.

1Why this instrument, versus standard methods

The standard toolchain for "does a model hear X" is offline: render audio, batch it through a Python pipeline, read a metric. Three properties of this rig change what questions are cheap to ask:

  • The sensor is the published model, verified, not an approximation. Filter design agrees with google/carfac at float64 precision (1.4e-12); the whole ear tracks the reference at 5.9e-8 per sample on real audio; the real-time SAI schedule is exactly zero-diff against the block reference. Every hair-cell time constant, damping ratio, and AGC pole is Lyon's published physiology — a hearing scientist can turn any of them and re-run recognition. Lesion studies (dead regions, hair-cell rot) are config, not surgery.
  • It runs live, inside the recording environment. Record a take, watch the percepts, get a verdict — the loop from "I wonder" to "measured" is minutes. Yesterday that loop ran ~20 times between breakfast and midnight, including three experiments that killed our own published claims. Offline pipelines make that cadence a week.
  • The data is yours and the confounds are physical. Every anomaly we hit traced to a nameable object: a hollow guitar body, a tuning offset, a Hz-denominated tolerance. When your dataset is takes you played, on instruments you own, the residuals have addresses.

2The instrument

Signal path: string → DI → CARFAC cascade (83 asymmetric resonators, two-cap hair cells, 4-stage AGC) → strobed temporal integration → SAI frame (place × lag) → percept (location + pose + features) → Monty evidence matching → verdict.

An auditory object is a path: location is (log₂ lag × 0.1 m, cochlear-place centroid × 0.004 m), so a melody is a curve, a drone is a cluster, and an octave is the same distance everywhere. Time is the saccade — the listener sits still and the sound's own evolution walks the object. Features at each node: pitch (log scale), a four-number harmonic timbre vector from the raw observation (precedent: Monty's CameraSM computes curvature from raw depth), level, salience.

What JSFX is, and why it's here

JSFX is REAPER's built-in scripting language (EEL2): plain-text DSP compiled just-in-time inside the DAW, sample-accurate, no build step — save the file and it is running on the live audio path. The cochlea + SAI port (lms_sai.jsfx, ~1700 lines) runs the full 83-channel cascade, strobe integration, pitch tracker, and a certain-only chord readout at ~30% of one core; a whole-ERB "lean" mode halves that. The reference schedule computes each SAI frame in one burst; the port amortises the identical arithmetic across the hop — proven bit-identical, so the plugin is the reference, rescheduled. This is the piece that makes the science interactive: the same verified ear that runs the offline rig is a window open next to the recording session.

3Validation: matching the other guys

Also on the record: the pitch tracker's first-peak-over-threshold rule (YIN's rule, applied to the SAI marginal) measures within 1.4 cents worst-case across E2–G4, where naive argmax errs by up to 3 369 cents; the chord-quality readout was grid-searched to zero wrong-quality frames in 4 759 across ten labelled takes, and abstains otherwise.

5Open questions (pre-registered where possible)

Next run, prediction on record

The width limb. 136 cents is wider than a semitone, so the mode question is unasked, not answered. Re-run at 80–90 cents: transposition and foils should hold, hollow-body major should still fail, and the solid-body major is the fork — it either starts failing (mode lives at a semitone) or survives on path evidence (mode is genuinely below the object threshold). Either outcome is a sentence in this paper.

  • The backwards row. Solid-body C-minor reads "confused" under both rulers while solid-body C-major reads correct — opposite to every other result. Bad take or best row; five minutes with the first five seconds of that take decides.
  • Polyphony. The sensor is winner-take-all per instant; chords and mixtures need per-row runner-up extraction — the same missing mechanism identified independently by the chord-quality study. Two problems, one mechanism: usually the sign it's the right mechanism.
  • Source-free identity. Recognition crossed guitars; does it cross to a sung melody? If yes, tune-identity in this frame is genuinely source-independent.
  • Recognition through hearing loss. Dead regions and hair-cell degradation are config in this cochlea. At what lesion does a known melody stop being findable? (No prior art found for object recognition through a lesioned cochlear model.)
  • The instrument as amp. The hollow body behaved as an analog processor whose signature survives DI (it's coupled into the string; the pickup senses only string). The same decomposition is a perceptual test bench for amp simulators — planned: DI → real Vox AC15 → our Vox-style sim, same riff, same units.
  • String compression. Attack pitch-sharpening (tension modulation) is a displacement meter the tracker reads in cents; graded-intensity "picking ladder" takes on both guitars yield the transfer curve of wood-as-compressor.
